card.title: When Things Made Sense
card.instruction: Perform the person you were before reality became complicated, using outdated certainty to explain each new impossibility.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When I was caretaker, this door opened into the staffroom. What's all this Thursday business?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It opens into next Thursday. My coat's still in there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Calendar's been fitted backwards. I'll turn it round.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now it's last Thursday. My coat hasn't arrived yet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wrong-size calendar. Fetch the old one. We never lost a coat to a properly fitted door.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 invokes the old caretaker's ordinary doorway, A3 treats temporal displacement as a backwards calendar, and A5 explains the failed fix as wrong-size equipment.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's next-Thursday coat problem causes A3's calendar reversal; B4's last-Thursday result causes A5's old-calendar request.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants the coat back and B4 gives the actual result of A's attempted repair.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's new date to double down on fitting the old ordinary component rather than accept the changed reality.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a former staffroom door and B2 its current temporal destination.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's properly-fitted-door certainty is earned by B4's failed calendar change and A1's caretaker identity.
